llm.summary: This web-development skill is mostly coherent, but its CloudBase auth examples can teach agents to accept unverified tokens as authenticated users.

dimensions.detail: Browser checks, build commands, CloudBase SDK use, and deployment tool references are purpose-aligned, but the CloudBase examples include an under-documented ap-shanghai region fallback and unsafe auth placeholder behavior.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is markdown-only with an MIT license, no executable scripts, no package install hooks, and alwaysApply is false.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The activation rules are scoped to web frontend work and refer to local sibling skills rather than fetching remote instructions; the main concern is insecure copyable guidance in the framework examples, not instruction hijacking.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No hidden persistence, background workers, credential scraping, tool replacement, or automatic privilege escalation behavior was found in the inspected files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's web, React/Vue/Vite, browser validation, and CloudBase integration purpose is coherent, but frameworks.md includes server-side auth examples that are labeled as token verification while authorizing based only on a non-empty token.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are prepared to review and correct the authentication snippets before using them. Do not copy the protected-route or AuthGuard examples into production unless token signature, issuer, audience, expiry, environment, and revocation/session state are verified by a trusted backend or supported CloudBase validation flow. Also configure the CloudBase region explicitly for your deployment.
llm.findings:
[SDI-4] unexpected: Confirmed: the NestJS AuthGuard example extracts a Bearer token, assigns it to request.user, and returns true without performing validation, which is not acceptable for an auth verification example.
[SQP-3] expected: Confirmed: a region value is expected for CloudBase setup, but the hardcoded ap-shanghai fallback is under-documented and should be made explicit or user-configured; this is low impact by itself.
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed in context: the Next.js and NestJS examples both contain presence-only token checks around protected resources. This supports Review because it is unsafe guidance, but it is not evidence of malicious execution or exfiltration.
